licences.notes: Written out from the printed pages by two independent readers, with a judge settling every difference and a sweep for the marks, then a fresh check until clean; every bar of every part adds up. The Italian translation, the notes printed only for it, and the stage directions are left out. Each Boy has his own line; the print puts two Boys on one staff in places (a note printed once for two Boys is sung by both; where their voices cross, they are told apart by the stems), and Pamina on the First Boy's staff. Bar 1 is a one-beat upbeat. Playback tempo from complete recordings: the median length of this scene, 5:55, from Klemperer 1964 (6:22), Toscanini 1937 (6:12), Haitink 1981 (5:55), Christie 1995 (5:50) and Nézet-Séguin 2018 (1:38 + 3:54, split at Pamina's entry); no recording splits it at the Allegro, so the Andante and the Allegro keep the proportion of Nézet-Séguin's recording, whose first track times the Andante alone.
